rendered:
The separated cathode powder was calcined in air at 600 °C[1] for 2 h[2] to remove surface coatings and carbon black (CB). 

Why: the authors saw an organic coating form on the NMC622 particles during the Cyrene-based separation, and suggested it may come from a reaction between NMC622 and Cyrene. TGA-DTG data show the coating loses ~3.3 wt% loss at ~350 °C[3] and CB loses ~4.1 wt% loss at ~550 °C[4], and both can be removed by calcining in air at 600 °C[5]. 

The XRD patterns before and after calcination were nearly identical with no impurity phases, so the layered structure was preserved.
